newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban bomb northern city, fail to retake another.
newsitem.headline: Taleban bomb northern city, fail to retake another.

text.p: Taleban warplanes bombed the northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Saturday, but the Islamic militia failed to dislodge opposition forces from a key town on the main road from Kabul to the north.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) said Taleban planes had mounted 60 bombing sorties against Mazar-i-Sharif from airbases in the southern city of Kandahar and Shindand in Herat province.
It said Taleban planes flying from the Soviet-built airbase at Bagram north of Kabul had also bombed targets in the Panjsher Valley, stronghold of opposition commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
The raids on Mazar-i-Sharif appeared to be retaliation for the heavy defeat suffered by Taleban forces there earlier in the week at the hands of local Shi'ite Moslem and Uzbek fighters.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the bombing, which came three days after a Taleban force of about 3,000 was driven from the city amid heavy casualties.

On Friday, an ethnic Uzbek commander named General Humayun Fauzi warned that any ground or air attack on Mazar-i-Sharif could have "dangerous" consequences for Taleban prisoners in the city, including Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammed Ghous and military commander for the north Mullah Abdul Razzak.
The Taleban conceded on Saturday it had lost the strategic town of Jabal-os-Siraj to Masood's guerrillas, cutting off a big Taleban force in the north from its base in the capital Kabul.
Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told reporters in the northern town of Pul-i-Khumri that Masood's forces were holding Jabal-os-Siraj, about 70 km (56 miles) north of Kabul.

Masood's men seized the town of Golbahar at the mouth of the Panjsher Valley on Friday and then took nearby Jabal-os-Siraj, at the foot of the Salang Pass which runs through the Hindu Kush mountains and is a crucial gateway between north and south.
Mutaqi had earlier said the Taleban had recaptured the town on Friday and reopened the road through the Salang Pass. He said fighting was still going on around the town on Saturday.

A 3,000-strong Taleban force, which crossed the Salang earlier this week to try to link up with Taleban fighters then in the northern capital of Mazar-i-Sharif, is now effectively isolated from its supply lines south of Jabal-os-Siraj.
Mutaqi said the Taleban force based in Pul-i-Khumri had repulsed an early morning attack on its positions south of the town of Aibak, the capital of Samangan province.

"The opposition launched an offensive at 7.00 a.m. (0230 GMT). They were beaten back and their dead bodies and burnt vehicles are still on the front line. One Taleban fighter counted more than 50 bodies," he told reporters.
He said the front line was some 50 km (31 miles) north of Pul-i-Khumri, just south of Aibak.
Opposition forces were shelling Taleban positions behind the front line when journalists visited the area on Saturday morning. It was not possible to reach the battle front.
Mutaqi said the Taleban had formed a new front line on the border of Badghis and Faryab provinces in northwest Afghanistan.
"The front line is on the border of Badghis and Faryab provinces. Badghis is entirely in our hands," he said.

The Taleban took four nothern provinces last week when an opposition Uzbek commander, General Abdul Malik, apparently defected to them. They were forced to relinquish their gains when their erstwhile ally turned on them.
The International Committee of the Red Cross said it had picked up over 100 bodies from the streets of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Mutaqi said he had no information about the Taleban fighters who had been driven out of Mazar-i-Sharif.

AIP said the Taleban were gathering thousands of fighters to reinforce their embattled frontlines. It said Islamic religious schools in neighbouring Pakistan had closed to allow 8,000 students to cross into Afghanistan to join the Taleban.
Witnesses said several busloads of slogan-chanting Afghan refugees left the southern Pakistani port city of Karachi for the border town of Quetta to join the Taleban.
